DomainGuard is off. New attempts are recorded only while traffic passes through its VPN.

The same access records shown beneath individual apps, combined into one list. Repeated attempts to the same destination update its existing record; this is not a separate row for every request. No additional recording setting is needed.

Filters use each app’s current default access, app type and enabled status. Apply lasts for this session; Set as default saves separate Recent traffic defaults, and Reset restores them. App filters do not change Hide allowed domains, hidden apps, sorting or the time window. For shared network identities, a record is included when any associated app matches all selected filters. Unidentified apps are shown only without app filters.

Newest first follows updated records while you are at the top; scrolling keeps your place. The time window moves with the clock.

Hide allowed domains uses the same filter as the app lists, keeping blocked, unknown and pending entries visible. It starts with your global display setting; changing it here affects this session only. It does not change recording or firewall rules.

The eye beside an app hides all traffic for its network identity from this view. Hidden apps lets you show it again. Apps sharing that identity are hidden together.

Domain colors and rule icons match the app lists. Tap a domain for Allow, Block or Copy. Where a network identity belongs to several apps, choose the app before adding a rule.

Only access observed and recorded by DomainGuard appears here. An IP address is shown when its domain is unknown. This can reveal activity from helper apps, but cannot establish which app triggered it.
